COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
BA1 No.29 of 2022
Hon'ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
Mr. Karan Anand, learned counsel for the
applicant.
 Mr. Pankaj Joshi, learned B. H. for the State.
Accused-Rajni Kohli has sought her release
on bail in connection with Case Crime/FIR No.0018
of 2021, u/s 420 and 120-B IPC, 66(C)/(D) of the
IT Act & 3/21, 4/22 of The Banning of Unregulated
Deposit Scheme Act, 2019, registered at P.S. Cyber
Crime, Dehradun, Distt. Dehradun.
It is argued by learned counsel that the
accused has been falsely implicated; she is
languishing in jail since 29.07.2021; she is a
Company Secretary by profession; she advised the
Directors of the company (Sumyth technology Pvt.
Ltd.); she has no concern with the offence; she did
not receive any money from the investors; in
another criminal cases, pending before NCR and
Bombay, she has been enlarged on bail; she is ready
to furnish the sureties; and she may be granted bail.
Learned counsel for the State opposed for bail
but fairly admitted that the applicant is a Company
Secretary.
Admittedly, the applicant is a Company
Secretary by profession; she is not named in the
FIR; there is no prima facie evidence on record that

she received the money from the investors directly;
as regard to the transaction from the account of one
Ram Ujagar is concerned, it is the submission of
learned counsel for the accused that the money
related to her advice.
It is a matter of evidence whether the
money, which was received by the accused from the
account of one Ram Ujagar, was actually a fee
related to the advice given by the accused as a
Company Secretary or not, but admittedly she is
Company Secretary by profession; in another
criminal matters, she has already been enlarged on
bail; charge-sheet has been submitted and now there
is no chance of tampering with the evidence;
accordingly, without going into merits of the case, it
is a fit case for bail at this stage.
The bail application is thus, allowed and the
applicant is directed to be released on bail on her
executing a personal bond and furnishing two
reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the Court concerned.
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.)
 08.04.2022
R.Bisht
